audit.why: TRICKY 7/10 fits an anti-mage laner Veigar still wins 53.84% over 1562 games by out-scaling at first item — the content layer frames early-Galio/late-Veigar correctly.
spikes[] is well-grounded: Galio 3-5 poke/sustain, his 6 being a roam spike not a kill spike, Veigar flipping at first item and dominating late. No change needed.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer chart rows 3-6 said Skill while content and packet give Galio 4-5 and Veigar from first item; breakdown.cooldowns had no digit; bleed bullets; P auto-reset tell and E-knockup Flash discipline unstated in the full layer.
audit.why: Kit: Galio E 11/10/9/8/7s dash knockup, W 18-14s taunt+shield, Q 11-7s projectile tornado, R 180/160/140s global; P Colossal Smash carries the autoReset flag. Veigar E 20s.
audit.corrected: Chart aligned with rewritten whys, real cooldowns added, auto-reset tell in dontsFull[2].d, Flash-for-knockup in dontsFull[0].d.

audit.why: 53.84% Emerald+ figure present; packet's chart-vs-WR defect resolves as early-Galio/late-Veigar scaling.

edits.before: Lost Chapter timing — Q-stack on cooldown and double-stack off cannon waves. The curve is the matchup.
edits.after: His tornado poke and W shield sustain keep the edge — Q-stack on cooldown, double-stack cannon waves.

edits.before: Primordial Burst online — anyone under half is now a math problem with one answer. Count R damage out loud.
edits.after: His R is a roam tool, not a kill button, but his poke edge holds — don't force a combo his E knockup can cancel.

edits.before: Luden's spike: cage-W-Q-R deletes squishies who touch the wall. Your zone is a courtroom now.
edits.after: Stacked Q starts one-shotting a tank-building Galio — the trade flips on your Luden's completion.

edits.before: Late Veigar IS the scaling argument: cage the choke, burst the carry, and let infinite AP write the closing statement.
edits.after: He's a utility tank with no burst — stacked AP deletes him through the W shield if E lands before Justice Punch.

edits.before: - Galio Justice Punch: matchup-defining — His dash knockup — he has no engage while it is down. It governs your forward steps. - E Event Horizon (self-cage) spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.
edits.after: - Galio Justice Punch: matchup-defining — 11s at rank 1 (7s max); he has no engage while it is down, so it governs your forward steps. - E Event Horizon (20s at rank 1) spent on poke is a death you scheduled. - Hold the R for the fight that decides something.

edits.before: Cage his step-up, W the edge-stun, Q-auto, and walk — a half-bar trade that also deposited three stacks into the curve.
edits.after: Cage where he must walk to farm — the edge stun into W-Q is your one clean trade, taken only while Justice Punch is down.

edits.before: That’s Galio’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: Hold your Flash for his E knockup, never for the damage — punished retreats start there.

edits.before: W-ing open ground on a moving target and trading uncaged 'just to stack' — Veigar without the wall is a piggy bank with a hat.
edits.after: His Colossal Smash auto-reset opens every trade — the wind-up is your step-back cue, and auto range is where his damage lives.

edits.before: Galio wins by landing Justice Punch, denying your pattern, and turning your every misstep into the all-in you hadn’t budgeted.
edits.after: Galio wins by shrugging your poke with W's shield, knocking up your combo with Justice Punch, and roaming on his global R.
